title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Generative video technology was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery by superimposing the faces of named Dutch public figures onto adult film footage. The material was hosted on a platform that monetized uploads through anonymous payments tied to view counts, creating a financial incentive for creation. The failure was deployment of the platform without systems to detect or prevent this use, and without human review of uploads before they reached 13 million monthly visitors.

The deepfake pornography violated existing revenge porn legislation, making it criminal. Victims discovered the content and filed complaints with authorities rather than the harm being caught by the platform. What is not established: whether the platform operator knew the content violated law, or whether the victims' legal actions resulted in convictions or removal of material.

This case shows how an image generation tool can be grafted onto an unmoderated distribution system. It required either content detection at upload, human review before publication, or legal intervention after the fact to prevent harm. None of these occurred at the deployment stage.

summary:
Multiple female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering they appear in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature the faces of Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government ministers, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos appalling and urged victims to file reports. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed to the NOS that they have filed complaints or are exploring legal options.

The deepfake pornography involves placing a celebrity's head onto footage of adult performers. Users who upload material receive anonymous payment based on video views. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake videos will emerge. Deepfake content falls under revenge porn legislation and is therefore criminal. Victims can file complaints with authorities, who may attempt to shut down the website, or pursue other options including mass claims and complaints to data protection authorities. Previously, presenter Welmoed Sijtsma made a documentary about her experience with such videos after a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort received a conditional sentence of 180 hours in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
